adjudication.rationale: The new “credential sync endpoint” path is not compatible with several call sites as implemented in this diff. The contract comment in `refreshOAuthTokens` says the endpoint response “should only contain the access token and expiry date”, but callers often rely on provider-specific fields and/or refresh token persistence: (1) Google sets `googleCredentials.expiry_date = token.expiry_date` (expects an `expiry_date` field) and then validates via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` (which, in sharing mode, only enforces `access_token` + some numeric field, not `expiry_date`), so an endpoint that returns `expires_in` won’t satisfy the code. (2) Zoom uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)`; in sharing mode `parseRefreshTokenResponse` accepts minimal fields and will fabricate `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if missing, which can cause incorrect refresh-token handling/rotation. (3) Salesforce calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` but in sharing mode it validates only the minimal schema and then persists `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ...}`—this can drop required fields like `instance_url` from the stored credential. These are correctness/data-loss issues grounded in the shown changes.
